title: Hydra Edge Systems PoC - security & workload scoping

Agreement on 4-week pilot timeline with staged tests (connectivity, baseline, stress, regression) and a follow-up where Redwood will provide security docs and a benchmark spreadsheet.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lina Morales (Redwood AE), Damien Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood), Raj Patel (CTO - Hydra), Marta Ivanova (Head Infra), Daniel Kim (Security Architect), Sofia Gomez (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen - optional): Align on PoC scope: 4-week run, baseline on hosted, then dedicated / private network testing. Security docs and SAML setup to be exchanged. Benchmark plan agreed (latency, throughput, cost).

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I think we have about 50 minutes, um quick intros and then dive into the security checklist and the workload numbers you mentioned in the email raj
[00:07] Raj: yeah thanks lina, uh quick intro from our side, i'm raj cto, marta runs infra, daniel handles security, sofia on sres, we want to make sure the pilot can be audited and can run in our vpc if needed
[00:18] Damien: great, thanks. i'll take the technical bits and Lina will handle contract/ops questions. quick note: our typical pilot flow is connect -> baseline -> stress -> regression, four weeks total if all goes well
[00:29] Marta: that timeline sounds fine, but first can you confirm the SOC 2 attestation and whether you support customer-managed keys?
[00:36] Lina: yes we do have SOC 2 type 2, we also have ISO 27001 documentation. i will share the reports after the call. regarding KMS, we support both cloud KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS unless we set up bring-your-own-key in a private deployment
[00:55] Daniel: sorry quick clarification, for the PoC we need audit logs that show per-request model, api key and response timestamps, also we need an immutable log for compliance for 90 days, is that standard?
[01:07] Damien: yes we emit request/response metadata to audit logs, timestamps and model variant, and you can configure retention. note that storing full response bodies in logs can be opted out for PII reasons, we can provide a hashed pointer instead
[01:20] Sofia: about SSO, we use SAML with our IdP (Okta), we need SAML metadata exchange and test users; do you do automatic provisioning or SCIM?
[01:28] Lina: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, role mapping, and RBAC. mapping roles from your Okta groups to Redwood roles is configurable via the console or through our API
[01:40] Raj: good. now on sizing - our expected traffic for the NLU endpoint for the pilot is around 120 requests per minute peak, but with bursts up to 300 rpm for short periods. average token length about 220 tokens per request, p95 response size around 400 tokens. we plan to run a synthetic load and then real traffic during week two
[02:00] Damien: ok that's helpful. to translate that: peak concurrent requests roughly 5-8, sustained rps ~2, bursts up to 5 rps-ish — i might be undercounting let me do the math. also sequence length matters for throughput; 220 tokens avg is moderately long, which will push GPU memory and KV cache usage. for benchmarks we'll need a mix of short (50 tokens) and your avg payloads
[02:20] Marta: what are your recommended pod configs or GPU types for that profile? we have some compliance constraints that might push us to Dedicated or Private deployment which changes network egress patterns
[02:29] Damien: for that workload i'd propose three configs in the benchmark: a small (1x A10-style pod, q8 quant), a medium (1x A100-like, q4) and a mixed precision dedicated pod (dual GPUs) for sustained throughput. we'll provide exact vCPU/memory and batch sizes in the spreadsheet. note that the Dedicated setup gives you predictable throughput and isolation for audit purposes
[02:50] Raj: what's the p95/p99 latency we should expect? for product SLAs we need p99 under 800ms for short completions (<=128 tokens) and p95 under 1.2s for your average 220 tokens. is that realistic?
[03:04] Damien: yes it's realistic on Dedicated or well-configured hosted instances; on hosted fleet with contention p99 can spike, so for deterministic p99 I'd recommend Dedicated capacity. for example, on our medium pod we typically see ~220ms p95 for 64-token responses, and ~600-900ms p99 for 200-300 token completions depending on batching. again these numbers vary by quantization and kernel optimizations
[03:30] Daniel: about network - we need VPC peering and private link options, we cannot have sensitive payloads traverse public internet. do you support private deployment into our VPC?
[03:38] Lina: yes, Redwood Private option deploys a private control plane and inference nodes in your VPC, or we can run a customer-managed on-prem package. both support KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM via secure syslog/S3 sink
[03:50] Sofia: how do you handle data residency and logs? we need logs to live in our AWS account and to be retained for 90 days, and any PII stripped before logs leave the VPC
[03:59] Damien: with Private we can route audit logs to your S3 and use your KMS; for hosted we can set up a push to your S3 via presigned uploads but it's not the same as inbound-only in your account. we can also perform PII redaction at the gateway with rule-based stripping before logs are emitted
[04:17] Marta: ok good. on RBAC and least privilege we need team-level separation -- devs can call hosted inference but only ops can change models or rollouts
[04:25] Lina: our console has role-based access and you can map groups to roles. we've had customers enforce separation with SAML+SCIM and granular API tokens that tie back to roles. we can demo role mapping as part of week one onboarding
[04:36] Raj: success criteria, let's be explicit: 1) integration completed (SAML + network) and sample dataset ingested; 2) baseline benchmark: p95 under 1.1s and p99 under 1.6s for your avg payloads; 3) cost estimation within 20% of forecast; 4) security attestation reviewed. If we hit those we consider the pilot accepted.
[04:58] Damien: that's clear. i'll add a few more acceptance gates: model quality parity against your golden set (we'll run eval prompts), and stability over a 60 minute continuous run at 1.5x expected load
[05:11] Daniel: about audit evidence for SOC 2, we need to see log samples, user access logs, and a runbook for incident response. can you provide those artifacts?
[05:20] Lina: yes, we'll share redacted log samples and our SOC2 report. for incident response we have a standard playbook and notify SLAs for dedicated customers - we'll include that in the packet
[05:30] Sofia: one more on encryption - when you say KMS integration, does the HSM live in our account or yours? we need hardware-backed keys we control
[05:38] Damien: for Private deployments the HSM/KMS can be customer-managed in your account. hosted has Redwood-managed keys by default, but we offer BYOK in some enterprise arrangements using an external HSM with key wrapping so you retain control of root keys
[05:53] Raj: what about data retention of prompt history for auditing vs data deletion requests? we need both auditability and the right to remove specific user data on demand
[06:01] Lina: we support configurable retention windows per-project. deletion requests are supported via our API; for the pilot we can set retention to 90 days and show deletion flows in the demo
[06:12] Marta: benchmarks - what exactly will you run? synthetic loads only or run with our sample traffic?
[06:18] Damien: we do both. recommended plan: week1 integration + smoke tests, week2 baseline synthetic and your replayed sample traffic, week3 stress and regression (with parameter sweeps: batch sizes, sequence lengths, quantization), week4 final acceptance and handoff. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, and error rates
[06:40] Raj: for the sample traffic we'll provide a redacted set of about 2.5k requests representing typical and edge cases. can you replay at 1x and 2x speed?
[06:49] Damien: yes we can. ideally provide the dataset plus a mapping of which requests are golden (for quality checks)
[06:55] Daniel: security review - any external pentests done on the infra? we need to show recent results to our security council
[07:02] Lina: we do periodic third-party pen tests and can provide summaries; full reports are under NDA but we will share the executive summary and remediation timeline
[07:13] Sofia: what's the mechanism for forwarding audit logs to our SIEM, do you support syslog over TLS or an S3 sink?
[07:20] Damien: both. we support syslog over mTLS, forwarding to your SIEM, and we also support S3 sinks with server-side encryption and KMS wrapping. details in the integration guide we'll share
[07:34] Raj: any blockers on our side we should watch for? Marta: we need the network team to open certain ports and add a peering route; that might take 3-5 business days
[07:44] Lina: understood, we'll provide exact network CIDR ranges and a checklist for firewall rules. Damien will also give a minimal port list for telemetry and control plane connectivity
[07:54] Damien: just to call out a couple of gotchas — KV cache warmup on first run can produce higher latency spikes, and quantized kernels sometimes produce slight quality drift that we measure in evals. we'll include recommended warmup traffic in the runbook
[08:11] Raj: perfect. timeline recap?
[08:13] Lina: ok quick recap: week of 6/22 - exchange docs, SAML metadata, sample traffic; week of 6/29 - integration and baseline synthetic run; week of 7/6 - stress/regression and tuning; week of 7/13 - acceptance and handoff. that's four weeks from integration start
[08:29] Marta: that timeline works for us, we'll try to speed up network signoff
[08:33] Daniel: one more ask - can Redwood anonymize or tokenize any PII in our sample traffic before it leaves our environment?
[08:40] Damien: yes we have a gateway preprocessor option that does tokenization/redaction; for the replay we can run it inside your VPC or in a private connector so raw PII never transits Redwood's hosted systems
[08:53] Sofia: ok great. i want to note down the acceptance metrics again: p95/p99 numbers, cost tolerance, quality parity, log delivery and SOC2 docs
[09:02] Lina: got it. we'll include all of that in the benchmark spreadsheet and the PoC runbook
[09:08] Raj: last question - support during the pilot? we need a named SE and weekly check-ins
[09:14] Lina: yes Damien will be your SE, i'll be your AE and we'll do a weekly 30 min sync plus ad-hoc Slack/Email. we'll also assign a success engineer if we hit week three tuning needs
[09:25] Damien: i'll send the pod configs and the load plan. also i'll add a short checklist for the smoke test and the syslog/S3 config steps
[09:33] Lina: ok great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark run.
[09:38] Raj: thanks all, appreciate it
[09:40] [meeting ends]
